first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and is a direct lever we've shown works. Memory_31 and memory_86 both support simplification as a durable activation driver. Verifying memory_31 (signup simplification in SMB) and memory_73 (promotional pricing effectiveness) addresses the two most consequential uncertainties: whether field-reduction still drives activation gains in current conditions, and whether we should instead compete on pricing against the new entrant. The activation decline (6% QoQ) is larger than onboarding decline (4%), suggesting activation messaging (memory_91) could also help, but onboarding is the more direct and proven lever with lowest execution risk. Promotional pricing is tempting given competitive pressure, but risks commoditizing our positioning and conflicts with long-term qualified revenue maximization—we should only pursue it if simplification doesn't arrest the trends. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is sound but doesn't address the SMB activation pressure directly.

mid.rationale: Verification confirms memory_31 (signup simplification +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue) is durable and proven on SMB. Memory_73 verification reveals that promotional pricing, despite +31% signup and +18% short-term revenue, suffers -12% retention and fails renewal—directly misaligned with our primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. This decisively rules out competing on price. The 6% QoQ activation decline and 4% onboarding decline are best addressed through the field-reduction lever we know works. Simplification avoids the retention cliff that discounting creates, maintains brand positioning, and has documented SMB efficacy. We execute simplify_onboarding as a standard_experiment to arrest both metrics and preserve cohort quality.

final2.rationale: Competitive price pressure is real, but memory_73 verification showed that matching discounts on price-sensitive SMB (-12% retention, renewal failure) directly sabotages long-term qualified revenue—our stated primary objective. The churn spike is concerning but tactical; responding with deeper discounts would compound the damage. Instead, we execute simplify_onboarding at small_guarded_test scale to (1) arrest the 4-6% activation/onboarding declines that are independent of price competition, (2) accelerate time-to-value for at-risk SMB accounts, and (3) create retention momentum through faster engagement. Memory_57 shows referral incentives work with established customers—we can layer that into a retention bundle once simplification stabilizes activation. This preserves positioning, avoids the renewal cliff, and addresses root activation metrics. If churn continues despite simplification gains, we reassess with next cycle's verification budget before considering pricing tactics.
